title: Resting Temperature Elevation Early-Illness Hint
dataSources: Continuous glucose (`cgm:glucose`), HRV (`hrv:reading`), mood check-ins (`mood:checkin`), ketone readings (`ketone:reading`), reaction-time trials (`reaction:trial`), sauna sessions (`sauna:session`), resting temperature (`temp:reading`), and meditation logs (`meditation:session`).
app: Biohacking telemetry from CGMs, HRV devices, ketone meters, mood and meditation journals, reaction-time apps, sauna logs, and health sensors streamed to Splunk HEC via APIs and scripted inputs.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=temp:reading metric="resting_temp"
| timechart span=1d avg(temp_c) as resting_temp_c
| eventstats avg(resting_temp_c) as baseline_temp_c
| eval delta_c=round(resting_temp_c-baseline_temp_c,2)
description: Highlights day-to-day resting temperature drift above your own baseline as an early sickness clue.
value: Small temperature elevations can matter more than a generic threshold when you know your personal normal well.
implementation: Capture a consistent daily resting temperature reading and compare it against your longer-term personal baseline.
visualization: Line chart of resting temperature and delta from baseline.
grandmaExplanation: It surfaces when your body temperature is running a little hotter than normal for you, which can hint at illness starting.
